summary: G0-G3 completed; R1 capability audit starts without an algorithm hypothesis or quality claim.
Two optimization frontends are executable and three feed-forward paths are adaptable. The first dirty-source run is noncanonical; clean-source fail-closed execution produced the canonical R1 run.

A real StreetGS checkpoint with 1,267,870 Gaussians and a ReconDrive output-schema fixture both round-trip through SceneIR v0 within the frozen tolerance and reload in fresh processes. This establishes only the representation interface, not reconstruction quality.

Across two development scenes and StreetGS/AD-GS, deviation produced stable measurable failure structure, but the preregistered analytic support certificate did not outperform lateral distance and its equal-distance residual rank was below gate. Learned support is rejected; distance remains a benchmark descriptor, not a universal validity certificate. Actor and forward probes remain effect evidence only.

The same real StreetGS SceneIR package produced exact world state, labels, chunk selection, 23-actor trajectories, and uint8 compiler-diagnostic RGB in three isolated fresh processes. No visual tolerance, GPU, training, or confirmation data was used. This passes the compiler determinism gate but is not a photorealistic source-camera quality result.

All 24 chunks, 23 actors and 1,267,870 primitives receive six typed provenance fields with exact fresh reload. Every current primitive is reconstructed, none is observed or generated, and absent sensor/view support remains unknown. Primitive identity must be composite over chunk_id and local source_index.

On all 48 frozen R3 rows, task-conditioned photo/geometry/semantic validity accepted only 8.3%/29.2%/8.3% but had zero accepted failures; the R3 single scalar reached 50% worst-case false-safe. Dynamics correctly accepted no cases because no independent dynamics verifier exists. This is a development proxy result, not confirmation calibration.

On 28 evidence-eligible pseudo-holes, every exact oracle proposal passed, every matched corrupted control failed, masked photo/depth errors recovered exactly, and outside-mask values and provenance were preserved. Four scene-0048/StreetGS actor cases had exactly zero actor-edit evidence and remain structural ABSTAIN. This validates only the observation-plane oracle upper-bound integration path.

Big-LaMa and SD-v1.5 each completed four frozen pseudo-holes twice with exact repeat hashes, finite nonzero masked change and exact outside-mask overlays. Big-LaMa was selected by the preregistered resource order at 428 MiB and 0.0374 seconds median versus SD at 2718 MiB and 0.786 seconds. This is capability only; no generated pixel is verified or baked.

On 28 matched pseudo-holes Big-LaMa produced no photo or geometry accepts; its semantic arm accepted 6 of 12 actor-evidence cases but one was false-safe, exceeding the frozen 0.10 ceiling. Dynamics correctly abstained on all 28. Resource and non-target gates passed, so the next isolated variable is the already capability-qualified SD-v1.5 generator with all verifier thresholds unchanged.

With every verifier threshold unchanged, SD-v1.5 produced zero photo accepts, only two geometry accepts out of 28, and the same one-in-six semantic false-safe as Big-LaMa; dynamics abstained on all cases. This rejects the second single-image generator and motivates an aligned cross-frontend reconstructed proposal, not threshold relaxation or per-case generator mixing.

Replacing single-image hallucination with a same-frame, same-edit reconstruction from the other frozen frontend yields independently valid photo and geometry arms: 10/28 and 3/28 accepts with zero false-safe. Semantic remains ineligible at one false-safe among six accepts and dynamics remains all-abstain. R10 may fuse only photo and geometry, and the shared sensor-support boundary remains explicit.

Fusing only independently valid photo and geometry arms yields 3 ACCEPT, 7 ABSTAIN and 18 REJECT over 28 cases, with zero false-safe and 9.52% verified mask area. All seven arm disagreements become ABSTAIN. Semantic, dynamics and verified trajectory length remain explicitly unsupported, so R11 must type-check assets before bake.

R11 packages the two jointly photo-and-geometry-valid route proposals as explicit sparse RGB chunks and reloads both exactly without a generator. The factor-incomplete actor hole becomes a bake ABSTAIN, producing zero actor and trajectory assets. R12 can validate only the resulting static logged-support sensor path until independently valid dynamic evidence exists.

Both baked static chunks replay twice with zero RGB error against their frozen source proposals, exact repeat hashes and exact frozen DeepLab label hashes. Peak GPU memory is 394 MiB and wall time 5.7 seconds. This closes only static sensor/perception consistency; all dynamic, event and calibration dimensions remain unsupported, so the next hypothesis uses the frozen SceneIR conformance package rather than manufacturing fields in the R11 package.

The frozen ReConDrive SceneIR fixture fresh-loads twice and produces exact actor world states, trajectories, camera calibration, actor semantic classes and AABB collision labels for two actors at two timestamps. This validates the interface contract but not real-scene scale or physical accuracy; H-R12-003 therefore moves to the real StreetGS scene-0230 package while retaining calibration/event abstentions where unsupported.

StreetGS scene-0230 fresh-replays all 23 actors and 4508 trajectory rows over 196 timestamps twice with exact actor, trajectory, semantic-class and 49588 AABB collision-label outputs in 4.38 seconds. Real-scene sensor calibration and events remain absent. R13 now tests whether the verified static patches can be lifted from their 2D bake format into sparse world-space route support.

The first lift creates 58273 deterministic points and retains zero V6 false-safe, but its estimated 0.01993 m2 area and zero visible pixels at every nonzero deviation show that R9 verifier-relative depth is not metric camera z. Threshold relaxation is disallowed. The next hypothesis changes only depth to bounded same-frame logged LiDAR while preserving the complete comparison and gate.

Changing only the transport depth to bounded logged LiDAR yields 57997 points over an estimated 19.13 m2. Both keyframes pass 0.5m, 1m, 2m and 3m lateral plus 2m forward under unchanged gates; both 5m cases fail with geometry MRE near 9. V6 retains 0/3 false-safe versus 23/28 naive and 28/28 Big-LaMa. H-R13-003 tests whether adjacent-keyframe union fixes the 5m support gap before adding target-view visibility logic.

The pre-registered 5cm two-keyframe union collapses 57997 input points to 5868, regresses common lateral support from 3m to 2m and worsens mean 5m geometry MRE from 9.0572 to 10.6579. This is an occlusion/visibility mechanism failure, not a tunable voxel-size or resource failure. H-R13-004 returns to the accepted per-frame chunks and uses only frozen target-view three-camera logged LiDAR to reject contradicted points before unchanged evaluation.

The frozen target-view LiDAR filter preserves the accepted 3m route and exact/safety contracts, but retains about 78% of old points at 5m and leaves geometry MRE at 9.03/9.41, so deletion-only visibility cannot synthesize newly exposed surfaces. Direct observation shows projected metric LiDAR z medians near 13m while the StreetGS 5m depth proxy median is only 1.2-1.3, so the proxy is not valid metric truth at that extrapolation. The route scope is therefore closed at the independently achieved 3m lateral/2m forward limit; H-R13-005 moves to the plan's untested typed actor edit dimensions instead of tuning visibility thresholds against a broken 5m proxy.

All three real-scene typed edits compile exactly over 23 actors and 196 timestamps: removal deletes 655 positive AABB collisions, +20m trajectory translation has zero centroid error, and the added density clone creates exactly 196 new source-clone collisions. All unaffected actor states and collision pairs remain exact, V6 is 3/3 ACCEPT with zero false-safe, and the stale-dependency naive arm is 3/3 false-safe. This establishes functional dependency closure but not sensor/perception behavior, so H-R13-006 now consumes the already frozen two-frontend actor-removal renders and frozen DeepLab model.

After correcting AD-GS RGB range handling, all four actor-removal renders show strong RGB locality (224x-498x enrichment and outside MAE below 0.0004), but full-frame DeepLab changes 6.3%-10.3% of labels outside the actor support; only one case reaches the frozen 2x perception-locality gate. Threshold relaxation is forbidden. H-R13-007 changes the mechanism to independently inferred target/static ROIs selected only from logged actor opacity, while preserving the same RGB and semantic change thresholds and retaining the H-R13-006 full-frame rejection.

The frozen 256px/128px ROI selector finds high-actor target tiles, but even the minimum non-overlapping static candidates contain 9.9%-37.3% actor pixels because the operation removes every actor. All four cases therefore fail the pre-registered static-factor denominator before any perception benefit can be claimed. No tile/stride sweep is allowed. H-R13-008 changes the edit granularity by selecting one StreetGS actor from frozen visibility/point-count metadata and rendering only its removal, with AD-GS and SceneIR identity binding explicitly abstaining.

StreetGS model index 2 is selected without outcome access from 12 actors visible at both frames and contains 13490 Gaussians. Its logged rerender exactly matches frozen R3 and its removal is strongly RGB-local, but DeepLab target label change is only 0%-0.068%, below the frozen 2% effect gate. This rejects Gaussian count as a perception-sensitivity selector. H-R13-009 removes every eligible actor in a complete fixed denominator and uses factorized ACCEPT/ABSTAIN coverage under identical thresholds, avoiding another heuristic or threshold sweep.

The complete 12-actor denominator identifies exactly one actor (StreetGS model index 0) that passes unchanged two-frame sensor/perception locality gates. Verified coverage is 1/12=8.33%; V6 abstains on 11 actors with zero false-safe, while naive all-accept is 91.67% false-safe. This is deliberately sparse, not a broad success claim. H-R13-010 now converts the identical scene-0242 checkpoint to SceneIR and binds accepted model index 0 to actor_0000 so typed removal and sensor/perception evidence share one scene and identity.

H-R13-010 passed same-scene checkpoint binding, model index 0 to actor_0000/12390-primitives identity, fresh replay, all unaffected factor checks, package/source immutability and inherited V6 false-safe zero. It was nevertheless correctly rejected because the preregistration conflated H-R13-009's 12 actors visible in both frames with the checkpoint converter's 27 total SceneIR actors. V6-F40 records the bookkeeping failure. H-R13-011 changes only the pre-registered total denominators to the deterministic frozen converter outputs 27/26, 5292/5096 and 68796/63700; all mechanisms and quality thresholds remain unchanged.

H-R13-011 separates the converter's 27 total actors from H-R13-009's 12 two-frame-visible evaluation actors and passes every frozen gate. Model index 0 binds to actor_0000/12390 primitives in scene-0242; typed removal yields 27→26 actors, 5292→5096 trajectories and 68796→63700 collision rows, with exact fresh replay and unaffected factors. Together with route, dynamic edit and sparse perception results, R13 closes on a bounded development scope and explicitly abstains beyond it. The V6.4 regression-test-set option is now exercised by H-PT1-001 using scene-0230 as contract source and scene-0242 as an independent downstream scenario.

The first H-PT1-001 run stopped before loading the heldout replay or constructing mutations because the consumer expected the shortened decision key accept_typed_dynamic_edits while the frozen H-R13-005 gate uses accept_typed_dynamic_edit_dependency_closure. V6-F41 records the cross-stage schema failure. The repair moves both exact accepted decision strings into the frozen config and changes no mutation, arm, metric, threshold, resource or evidence contract; H-PT1-001 remains active for an independent rerun.

On the independent scene-0242 actor-removal episode, Real-only detects 0/4 frozen stale-factor regressions with false-safe 1.0, naive synthetic detects only stale actor_states (1/4) with false-safe 0.75, and the V6 verified compiled contract detects 4/4 with false-safe zero while all three accept the clean episode. Exact repeated evaluation holds. This is regression-test utility only. H-PT2-001 now tests whether recomputed typed-edit labels improve a minimal CONTINUE/BRAKE risk admission policy on whole-scene heldout scene-0255.

H-PT2-001 passes its incomplete numeric gate and defeats naive stale-label training, but Real-only also reaches heldout balanced accuracy 1.0 and false-safe zero despite zero positive training examples. The signed-clearance feature is exactly the verifier statistic, so the model family receives the answer boundary and cannot prove post-training data utility. V6-F42 records the leakage. H-PT2-002 preserves data and labels but exposes only raw relative forward/lateral positions, makes one-class policies constant, and adds a mandatory false-safe reduction gate versus both Real-only and naive.

H-PT2-002 removes verifier-statistic leakage and makes both Real-only and naive constant-CONTINUE with heldout false-safe 1.0. V6 learns a 3.0m/0.5m raw-position rectangle, reduces false-safe to 0.1122 and keeps safe-route completion 1.0, but misses the strict <=0.05 and >=0.95 gates. All 11 misses are exactly the 3m clones whose transformed feature is 1e-13 to 5e-13 above 3.0. V6-F43 records the numeric contract failure. H-PT2-003 adds only 1e-9m feature canonicalization while preserving labels, grids and gates.
